english: where $\{t\}=t-[t]$ and $[t]$ denotes the greatest integer less than or equal to $t$. Let $\alpha$ be the number of points of the interval $(0,50)$ at which $f$ is discontinuous, and let $\beta$ be the number of points of the interval $(0,50)$ at which $f$ is not differentiable. Then the value of $\alpha+\beta$ is ______.
hindi: माना कि $f:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}$ इस प्रकार परिभाषित है

जहाँ $\{t\}=t-[t]$ है तथा $[t]$, $t$ से कम या उसके बराबर महत्तम पूर्णांक को दर्शाता है। माना कि $\alpha$ अन्तराल $(0,50)$ के उन बिन्दुओं की संख्या है जिन पर $f$ असतत है, तथा $\beta$ अन्तराल $(0,50)$ के उन बिन्दुओं की संख्या है जिन पर $f$ अवकलनीय नहीं है। तब $\alpha+\beta$ का मान ______ है।
solution: Let $p(x)=\sin\frac{\pi x}{2}\sin\frac{\pi x}{3}$ (smooth). Between integers $f$ is smooth, so only integers $n=1,\dots,49$ matter
Near $n$: $f=p(x)(x-n+1)$ on the left, $f=p(x)(x-n)$ on the right. Left limit $p(n)$, right limit and value $0$
So $f$ is continuous at $n$ iff $p(n)=0$ iff $2\mid n$ or $3\mid n$
If $p(n)=0$: left derivative $p'(n)\cdot1$, right derivative $p'(n)\cdot0=0$; differentiable iff $p'(n)=0$ iff $n$ is a double zero of $p$ iff $6\mid n$
Integers in $1..49$ divisible by $2$ or $3$: $24+16-8=32$; by $6$: $8$
solution_full: Write $p(x)=\sin\left(\frac{\pi x}{2}\right)\sin\left(\frac{\pi x}{3}\right)$, a differentiable function on $\mathbb{R}$, so $f(x)=\{x\}p(x)$.
On each open interval $(n,n+1)$, $\{x\}=x-n$ is a polynomial, so $f$ is differentiable there. Only the integers $n=1,2,\dots,49$ need checking.
Continuity: $\lim_{x\to n^{-}}f(x)=p(n)$ and $\lim_{x\to n^{+}}f(x)=0=f(n)$. Hence $f$ is continuous at $n$ iff $p(n)=0$.
$p(n)=0$ iff $\sin\frac{\pi n}{2}=0$ or $\sin\frac{\pi n}{3}=0$, i.e. iff $n$ is divisible by $2$ or by $3$.

Differentiability at such $n$: left derivative $=\left[(x-n+1)p(x)\right]'_{x=n}=p(n)+p'(n)=p'(n)$; right derivative $=\left[(x-n)p(x)\right]'_{x=n}=p(n)+0=0$. So $f$ is differentiable at $n$ iff $p'(n)=0$.

$p'(n)=\frac{\pi}{2}\cos\frac{\pi n}{2}\sin\frac{\pi n}{3}+\frac{\pi}{3}\sin\frac{\pi n}{2}\cos\frac{\pi n}{3}$. If exactly one of the sines vanishes, the surviving term is non-zero (the cosine of a zero of sine is $\pm1$). If both vanish ($6\mid n$), $p'(n)=0$. So $f$ is differentiable at $n$ iff $6\mid n$.
Counting in $\{1,\dots,49\}$: multiples of $2$: $24$; of $3$: $16$; of $6$: $8$. Divisible by $2$ or $3$: $24+16-8=32$.
$\beta$ = discontinuity points ($17$) + continuous but non-differentiable points ($32-8=24$) $=41$.
originality_note: New: the fractional part is multiplied by a product of two sines with different periods, so continuity at an integer needs a zero of the product and differentiability needs a double zero; the count becomes inclusion-exclusion on divisibility by 2, 3 and 6 (way 2). Closest known: continuity of [x] sin(pi x) or {x} sin(pi x) type products. Different because: three classes of integers behave differently and the answer needs a divisibility count.
key_step: At an integer n, continuity iff p(n) = 0 and differentiability iff p'(n) = 0 (double zero), giving the classes 'coprime to 6', 'divisible by 2 or 3 but not 6' and 'divisible by 6'.
justification: Two ideas linked: one-sided limits and derivatives of {x}p(x) at integers, then an inclusion-exclusion count with no options. Same kind of demand as 2023-P2-Q6 (L3) on [4x] times a polynomial; lighter than 2026-P2-Q14 (L4).

concept_use.Continuity and Differentiability of func: Product rule for the one-sided derivatives of (x-n+1)p(x) and (x-n)p(x) at n; differentiability iff p'(n) = 0.
{x} jumps from 1 to 0 at each integer, so f is continuous at n only when p(n) = 0.

stem_review: Read as a student: f has domain and codomain, {t} and [t] are defined, alpha and beta are counts on the open interval (0,50), one reading. Checked by computer that alpha = 17, beta = 41 (numeric one-sided derivatives at every integer). Answer 58, a positive 2-digit integer. Changed: No change.
